title: A Noetherian domain is N-1 from a normal principal open and N-1 maximal localizations
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with fraction field $K$. If some nonzero $f\in A$ has normal localization $A_f$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is N-1 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$, then the integral closure of $A$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is finite as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], i.e. $A$ is N-1.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), lines 45482-45539, implication (1)+(2) => N-1

proof.text: For each maximal ideal use its N-1 hypothesis to construct a finite intermediate algebra normal at all primes above it.
Patch these local approximations using the normal principal open to obtain a finite intermediate algebra B whose every prime localization is integrally closed.

Apply Mathlib's maximal-localization criterion to obtain IsIntegrallyClosed B. If x is integral over A, its monic equation also has coefficients in B; the fraction field of B is K, so integrally closedness puts x in B. Together with B contained in the integral closure this proves equality. Transfer Module.Finite along that equality and unfold IsN1.
